reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — not employer/local approval
experience_basis: Current local work-rule evidence plus SFS-O01-O08 cross-source synthesis
findings: The course may test being checked in and ready by call time, but it should not teach one national minutes-early rule. Exact arrival, check-in and reporting procedures remain call-specific.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence synthesis — practitioner review still required
experience_basis: Current local work-rule evidence plus cross-source assignment/reassignment synthesis
equipment_jurisdiction_context: General stagehand task completion, availability and reassignment
findings: Report-back instead of self-assignment is well supported as a transferable work-control pattern. Preserve the qualifier that break, standby, reassignment and release procedures vary by call, employer, local and CBA.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — not specialist authorization
experience_basis: Stagehand hazard/authority research and Fundamentals authenticity audit
equipment_jurisdiction_context: Unfamiliar or specialized work across live-event departments
findings: The existing scenario is appropriately non-operational: state the limitation and seek instruction/another assignment. It must not imply that one demonstration, observation or course completion authorizes controlled work.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted curriculum audit — practitioner validation required
experience_basis: Cross-department work-control logic; no universal external rule identified
equipment_jurisdiction_context: Unknown production cable across lighting/audio/video/power/data contexts
findings: Keep this as a Crew Blueprint work-control boundary: do not move an unfamiliar/unreleased cable merely because it appears idle. Before stronger publication treatment, obtain practitioner review across departments so local cable-ownership conventions are represented accurately.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted citation audit — not employer PIT training
equipment_jurisdiction_context: Powered industrial trucks within applicable federal general-industry scope
findings: The learner-facing boundary is supportable when explicitly limited to covered powered industrial trucks. Do not generalize the rule to every powered machine, lift or cart used in event production.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted curriculum audit — site/accessibility practitioner review required
experience_basis: OSHA walking-surface baseline plus venue/site work-control logic
equipment_jurisdiction_context: Venue/event route ownership, access and public/worker pathways
findings: Retain the conservative rule that visible physical access does not prove route approval, but do not attribute it to OSHA 1910.22. Venue access, public accessibility, egress, fire-code and AHJ layers require separate treatment.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence synthesis — department practitioner review still required
experience_basis: Operational call-cycle research and local work-rule context
findings: The course should continue to distinguish appearance/idleness from actual release. Exact release authority and terminology vary by department and production, so practitioner review remains appropriate before treating this as universal language.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — not wage/hour or CBA advice
experience_basis: Operational call-cycle/local evidence plus existing egress claim
equipment_jurisdiction_context: End-of-call cleanup, handoff, release and sign-out
findings: The scenario correctly separates main-task completion from call release and keeps egress clear during cleanup. Exact sign-out, timekeeping and release procedures remain employer/local/CBA/jurisdiction specific.
